frozen: 2026-10-29, before any attention feature was computed for any event and before any Reddit post beyond the plan's coverage sample was downloaded
owner_instruction: Yes to all (handoff/github-finds/PLAN_v2.md decision 2: run the Reddit attention study on 2020-2023 history)
prior_look: handoff/github-finds/PLAN_v2.md section 2 counted, for 23 sampled events, whether any r/wallstreetbets title named the ticker (10 of 23); no outcome column was read
question: On US stocks that just closed 30% or more higher, does retail attention on r/wallstreetbets add out-of-time discrimination to LEARNER v2.4's own 33 features, for its headline statement (the next session closes 10% lower, on its own) and its companion (the 5-session plan ends 10% down, on its own)?

reddit.source: Arctic Shift archive API, https://arctic-shift.photon-reddit.com/api/posts/search, subreddit wallstreetbets, fields created_utc and title only
reddit.build: build.py pages through each UTC day; every day file is stored gzipped under data/raw/reddit/wsb/ (git-ignored) and its sha256 recorded in results/REDDIT_MANIFEST.json before run.py reads it

matching.rule: a title names ticker T when it contains T as a whole token (no letter or digit on either side), case-sensitive, optionally prefixed by $
dollar_only: tickers of one or two letters
any title whose letters are more than half upper case (shouting titles), where only $T counts

timing: an event's signal session d is the +30% close; LEARNER v2.4 forecasts after that close. Every feature uses posts created before d at 20:00 UTC (the US close in summer, an hour before it in winter)

blocks.BASE: LEARNER v2.4's 33 features exactly as in the event file

features.wsb_pre5: log(1 + posts naming the ticker created from d-5 00:00 UTC to d 00:00 UTC)
features.wsb_day: log(1 + posts naming the ticker created from d 00:00 UTC to d 20:00 UTC)
features.wsb_surge: log((day count + 1) / (mean daily count over d-30 00:00 .. d 00:00 + 1))
features.wsb_any: 1 when any post named the ticker from d-5 00:00 to d 20:00 UTC

blocks.SETTLE: not part of v1 (fails-to-deliver data needs its own feasibility count; PLAN_v2 made it optional)

folds.note: TA_HISTORY_v1's folds; 2021 (the meme-stock year) is in both fits and in no score set

model: as TA_HISTORY_v1: penalised logistic regression, standardised on the fold's fit rows, intercept precision 1/1.5^2, slope precision 16; nothing tuned
metrics: as TA_HISTORY_v1: per-fold AUC, pooled by positive-negative pairs; paired delta AUC(BASE + ATTN) - AUC(BASE); week-cluster bootstrap, 2,000 resamples, seed 20261029; Brier gain beside it

decision_rule.adds: Holm over the two at 0.05 rejects delta <= 0 and the pooled Brier gain over BASE is above zero
decision_rule.otherwise: DOES NOT ADD for that statement

descriptive: coverage of each feature by year
use: a block that ADDS becomes a candidate for a frozen LEARNER v2.5, considered only at v2.4's first claim look (30 populated sessions); a live version that reads the archive nightly needs the owner's approval, already given conditionally (PLAN_v2 decision 3). Nothing here changes v2.4, any ledger, register or frozen protocol
counted_trial: research/QUANT_GRADE/trials/ATTENTION_HISTORY_v1.json (2 variants, Holm), its result in ATTENTION_HISTORY_v1_result.json
limitations: titles only; comments and other subreddits are not read
a third-party archive: posts deleted before archiving are missing
the meme-stock era (2021) is fit-only; 2022-2023 attention is lower, which can only shrink the gain
a ticker that is an English word can still match by accident
